title: EO 14173 revokes Executive Order 11246
what: The affirmative-action executive order for federal contractors was revoked in January 2025; [OFCCP](#term:ofccp)'s implementing regulations followed in 2026 (ch-004) [86](#cite:86) [55](#cite:55).

title: EEOC removes its 2023 AI-in-selection technical assistance
what: The May 2023 document stating that [algorithmic tools](#term:algorithmic-screening) are selection procedures under the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) was taken down; the Title VII rules it restated did not change [35](#cite:35) [36](#cite:36).

title: California automated-decision-system regulations take effect
what: Civil Rights Council FEHA regulations define ADS, extend liability to agents, treat anti-bias testing as a defence factor and require four-year [record retention](#term:applicant-record-retention) [40](#cite:40).

title: OFCCP publishes three final rules; EO 11246 regulations rescinded effective 2026-10-26
what: 41 CFR parts 60-1, 60-2, 60-3, 60-4, 60-20, 60-40, 60-50 and 60-999 removed (91 FR 54444); [Section 503](#term:section-503) narrowed (threshold \$20,000; 7% goal and self-identification rescinded) and [VEVRAA](#term:vevraa) updated (threshold \$200,000) effective 2026-09-21 [86](#cite:86) [55](#cite:55).

title: Illinois AI-in-employment amendment in force; clarifying rules withdrawn 2026-06-02
what: Public Act 103-0804 bars discriminatory AI use and requires notice; IDHR's proposed rules were withdrawn and postponed [38](#cite:38).

title: Colorado AI Act effective date (delayed from 2026-02-01)
what: Superseded: the Act was repealed and reenacted by SB 26-189 before this date and never took effect (ch-027). SB25B-004 had moved the date and amendments were expected in the 2026 session [39](#cite:39).

title: SkillBridge employer obligations added
what: The August 2024 MOU sets a minimum annual intake by employer size and a 75% qualifying-offer standard (85% goal) [74](#cite:74).

title: California SB 642 clarifies "pay scale" in postings
what: Amends the [posting law](#term:pay-range-posting-law) and extends the recovery period; one of thirteen state posting laws plus DC [76](#cite:76).

title: Delaware pay-range posting law takes effect (26+ employees)
what: Joins the posting-law states [76](#cite:76).

title: Federal Fair Chance Act applies to contractors
what: No criminal-history inquiry before a conditional offer for positions under a federal contract; [cleared](#term:security-clearance) and national-security positions excepted [48](#cite:48).

title: EO 14236 revokes the $15 federal-contractor minimum wage order (EO 14026)
what: DOL no longer enforces EO 14026 or 29 CFR part 23; EO 13658 remains for 2015–2022 contracts at \$13.65 from May 11, 2026 [102](#cite:102) [101](#cite:101).

title: SCA health-and-welfare rate set at $5.55 per hour
what: WHD's July 2025 rate; \$5.09 where EO 13706 applies; Hawaii \$2.42/\$1.96 [101](#cite:101).

title: GAO extends the key-personnel notification duty to protesters (Orion Government Services)
what: An offeror with actual knowledge of a key person's unavailability must notify the agency; the proposal is unacceptable otherwise; the Court of Federal Claims (Golden IT, 2022) reads the duty more narrowly [108](#cite:108) [109](#cite:109).

title: Contractor compensation cap $671,000 for 2025
what: Prior cap times the [ECI](#term:employment-cost-index) change; estimated \$695,000 for 2026; secondary figure pending the OFPP determination [107](#cite:107).

title: DCSA moves industry timeliness reporting from fastest-90% to all-case averages
what: From FY2026 Q3 the industry figures are averages of all cases under PMIG-aligned reporting: [Secret](#term:secret) 197 days, [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) 243; the earlier 156 and 227 (fastest 90%) are not comparable [126](#cite:126) [125](#cite:125).

title: DFARS 252.223-7004 Drug-Free Work Force reserved
what: The DoD clause requiring contractor [drug-testing](#term:drug-free-workplace) programs on sensitive work is reserved at the May 7, 2026 DFARS change; the FAR drug-free workplace program (subpart 26.5, clause 52.226-7) remains and requires no testing [134](#cite:134) [135](#cite:135).

title: H-1B $100,000 entry restriction extended twelve months; collection paused by court order
what: A new proclamation effective September 21, 2026 extends the September 2025 restriction on entry of certain [H-1B workers](#term:h-1b) without a \$100,000 payment; the District of Massachusetts vacated the implementing policy on June 8, 2026 (California v. Mullin) and the First Circuit denied a stay on July 24, 2026, so the payment is not being collected while the appeal proceeds [142](#cite:142) [143](#cite:143).

title: USCIS proposes a $103,265 fee on H-1B cap-subject petitions
what: Proposed rule (91 FR 54817; docket USCIS-2026-0298) adding the [fee](#term:fee) at filing, in addition to all other fees and to any proclamation payment; comments closed September 24, 2026 with 11,706 received [141](#cite:141).

title: Trusted Workforce 2.0 milestones through FY2028
what: [eVetting](#term:nbis) for preliminary determinations August 2026 and full agency adoption October 2026; the Individual Engagement Platform's self-reporting and five-year [questionnaire](#term:sf-86) update September 2026; full [continuous-vetting](#term:continuous-vetting) enrolment September 2028 [54](#cite:54); NBIS roadmap: eInterview FY27 Q2, eVetting for low and moderate tiers FY27 Q4, [TW 2.0](#term:trusted-workforce-2) full operating capability FY28 Q1 [125](#cite:125).

title: GAO finds clearance timeliness statistics unreliable; DCSA calculation corrected from FY2025
what: 63 percent of 305 statistics reviewed were inaccurate or incomplete; [DCSA](#term:dcsa)'s method understated [processing time](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) from 2020 to 2024; four recommendations to ODNI [56](#cite:56).

title: California AB 692 bars most training-repayment and stay-or-pay terms
what: For contracts entered after January 1, 2026, repayment obligations for leaving before a date are unlawful except for transferable credentials under a separate, at-cost, prorated agreement, [signing bonuses](#term:signing-bonus) on stated conditions, government loan programs and approved [apprenticeships](#term:registered-apprenticeship); \$5,000 or actual damages, injunction and fees [167](#cite:167).

title: FTC accedes to the vacatur of the Non-Compete Clause Rule
what: By a 3–1 vote the Commission dismissed its appeals in Ryan LLC v. FTC and Properties of the Villages v. FTC and accepted the vacatur; [noncompetes](#term:noncompete-agreement) return to state law [169](#cite:169).

title: NLRB general counsel memoranda on stay-or-pay provisions rescinded
what: The two memoranda that treated [stay-or-pay](#term:stay-or-pay-provision) and [training-repayment terms](#term:training-repayment-agreement) as unlawful under the NLRA were rescinded by the current general counsel; the CFPB position stands [168](#cite:168) [166](#cite:166).

title: IRS revises the section 127 FAQs; loan repayment permanent, $5,250 indexed after 2026
what: FS-2026-10 removes the January 1, 2026 sunset on tax-free student-loan payments after the 2025 amendments, states that the \$5,250 limit is adjusted for the cost of living for taxable years after 2026, and requires employers to notify employees of the program [174](#cite:174).

title: DOL rescinds the nondisplacement rule (29 CFR part 9) after EO 14148 revoked EO 14055
what: The [successor-contractor](#term:successor-contractor) [right of first refusal](#term:nondisplacement) is gone: EO 14148 of January 20, 2025 revoked EO 14055, the implementing FAR clause was never issued, and 29 CFR part 9 is removed and reserved effective December 22, 2025 [186](#cite:186). (Corrects the sweep-3 note t-3007, which had attributed the revocation to EO 14236.)

title: DOJ and FTC replace the 2016 HR antitrust guidance with worker-market guidelines
what: [No-poach agreements](#term:no-poach-agreement) illegal without harm and prosecutable criminally; wage coordination is wage-fixing; [non-solicit terms](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) within a collaboration judged on effects only if collateral and reasonably necessary; information sharing a risk [187](#cite:187).

title: Colorado repeals and reenacts its AI Act as SB 26-189, effective 2027-01-01
what: After xAI sued on April 9, 2026 and DOJ filed a companion complaint, a stipulated order of April 27 barred enforcement of SB 24-205; the replacement signed May 14 drops impact assessments and Attorney General disclosures for notice-based duties on [automated decision-making technology](#term:automated-employment-decision-tool) in consequential decisions, including employment: notice before use, a description of the decision and the tool's role within 30 days of an adverse outcome, meaningful human review, three-year records, Attorney General enforcement after a 60-day cure notice (the cure right expiring 2030-01-01) [222](#cite:222) [221](#cite:221).

title: Washington voids all noncompetes from 2027-06-30 and folds repayment and forfeiture terms into the ban
what: ESHB 1155 (Chapter 149, Laws of 2026) makes every [noncompetition covenant](#term:noncompete-agreement) void and unenforceable from June 30, 2027 regardless of signing date; the definition reaches provisions that require repayment or forfeiture because a person works in their chosen field, excepting educational-expense agreements that expire within 18 months of the start date; [nonsolicitation terms](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) survive with the customer restriction capped at 18 months; employers must notify affected workers by October 1, 2027; penalty the greater of actual damages or \$5,000 plus fees [210](#cite:210).

title: New York's Trapped at Work Act narrowed and postponed to 2027-02-13
what: Signed December 19, 2025; the chapter amendment of February 13, 2026 limits the Act to employees, postpones it a year and sets the exceptions: bonuses and relocation assistance unless termination was for a reason other than misconduct or the job was misrepresented, tuition for a transferable credential under conditions, voluntary property sales or leases, sabbatical terms and collective agreements; fines \$1,000–\$5,000 per violation enforced by the Labor Commissioner; no private action [212](#cite:212) [211](#cite:211).

title: Virginia and Maine join the posting states; Connecticut follows on 2026-10-01
what: Virginia (from July 1, 2026; all employers) requires a wage or salary range in every public and internal posting and bans [salary-history inquiries](#term:salary-history-ban), with a private right of action after a 15-day cure notice; Maine (from July 29, 2026; ten or more employees) requires a pay range in every posting; Connecticut PA 26-12 (from October 1, 2026; all employers) requires the wage or wage range and a benefits description in every advertisement; Delaware's law (more than 25 employees) follows on September 26, 2027 [223](#cite:223) [224](#cite:224).

title: Tennessee voids noncompetes for workers earning under $70,000
what: HB 1034, signed May 7, 2026, applies from July 1, 2026; above the threshold the common-law reasonableness test continues; the tracker carrying it is a vendor page and the act is a todo [209](#cite:209).

title: New York State limits employer credit checks
what: A statewide law effective April 18, 2026 joins New York City's 2015 ordinance; exceptions include police, positions requiring a [security clearance](#term:security-clearance), trade-secret and digital-security roles and fiduciary roles above \$10,000; Massachusetts's limit took effect January 1, 2025 [218](#cite:218).

title: FAR overhaul enters rulemaking; Part 37 proposed for reorganisation
what: Four proposed rules published June 23, 2026 (comments due July 23) begin Phase Two; FAR Case 2026-002 rewrites Part 37 with no stated change of policy (definitions and the management-oversight subpart removed; performance-based acquisition in 37.1; other policies in a new 37.8; [inherently governmental functions](#term:inherently-governmental-function) moved from 7.5 to 37.3) and the Council is considering relocating every provision and clause to a new subpart such as 52.4; Parts 19, 22 and 44 were not among the first four rules; the Phase One deviations, including Part 22, remain the working text [228](#cite:228) [227](#cite:227) [229](#cite:229).

title: H-1B payment litigation: two courts disagree; no appellate merits decision
what: The District of Columbia court upheld the proclamation on December 23, 2025 in the Chamber of Commerce and AAU case and the plaintiffs appealed to the D.C. Circuit on December 29 [226](#cite:226); the District of Massachusetts vacated the implementing policy on June 8, 2026 and the First Circuit denied a stay on July 24 [143](#cite:143); as of September 2, 2026 USCIS was not collecting the payment and neither appeal had been decided [225](#cite:225); the separate \$103,265 [fee](#term:fee) proposal (ch-018) is not in effect.

title: HB331 (2023) salary-history inquiry ban died in committee
what: HB331, which would have barred employers from requesting a prospective employee's wage history except in certain circumstances and added a voluntary-disclosure clause to § 25-1-30, was read first time and [referred](#term:referral-hiring) to House Commerce and Small Business on 2023-04-18 and died in committee; no 2024–2026 successor was located [238](#cite:238).

title: SB49 (2025) public-employer ban-the-box bill indefinitely postponed
what: SB49, which would have barred the State, its agencies and political subdivisions as employers from inquiring into arrest or conviction history before a conditional offer, was indefinitely postponed in the Senate on 2025-05-06; private employers were outside its scope [254](#cite:254).

title: Alabama Department of Labor renamed Alabama Department of Workforce (statutory effective date)
what: SB247 (2024), the Alabama Workforce Transformation Act, renames the Department of Labor the Department of Workforce and transfers Commerce's workforce programs other than AIDT to it, effective October 1, 2024, with full implementation not later than October 1, 2025 [266](#cite:266).

title: Department of Workforce name change takes effect operationally
what: The Governor's release of 2025-01-31 states that on February 1, 2025 the Alabama Department of Labor officially becomes the Department of Workforce, with its first Secretary of Workforce named [266](#cite:266).

title: Alabama Apprenticeship Tax Credit expires
what: ADOR states 'This credit expired on Dec. 31, 2024.'; no extension or replacement for tax years 2025 onward was found as of 2026-10-22 [263](#cite:263).

title: Alabama employer childcare tax credit window opens (2025–2027)
what: Act 2024-303 takes effect January 1, 2025 for tax years beginning on or after that date and ending December 31, 2027; ADOR rule 810-3-135-.05 opened first-come reservations on March 1, 2025 [267](#cite:267).

title: Alabama Jobs Act sunset for new project agreements
what: Under § 40-18-382 as amended by HB241 (2023), Jobs Act incentives are unavailable to qualifying projects whose project agreements are not executed on or prior to July 31, 2028 [260](#cite:260).

title: Innovate Alabama Supplemental Grant applications closed
what: On 2026-10-22 the Supplemental Grant Program page stated 'Applications are currently closed' and 'Stay tuned for details on upcoming rounds' [261](#cite:261).

title: DFARS CMMC rule takes effect; Phase 1 begins
what: The DFARS rule published 2025-09-10 (90 FR 43560) took effect 2025-11-10, making CMMC status a condition of award and starting the 32 CFR 170.3(e) phase clock [306](#cite:306) [305](#cite:305).

title: CMMC Phase 2 begins
what: Phase 2 'Begins one calendar year following the start date of Phase 1' under 32 CFR 170.3(e)(2); with Phase 1 on 2025-11-10, the date follows arithmetically [305](#cite:305). ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker))

title: CMMC full application under DFARS
what: The DFARS rule applies the requirement to all offerors on applicable solicitations 'Beginning three years and one day after the effective date of the rule' [306](#cite:306).

title: OFCCP rescission of EO 11246 implementing regulations effective
what: The final rule at 91 FR 54444 removes 41 CFR parts 60-1, 60-2, 60-3, 60-4, 60-20, 60-40, 60-50 and 60-999 and amends part 60-30, effective 2026-10-26 [308](#cite:308).

title: VEVRAA and Section 503 regulation modifications effective
what: The [VEVRAA](#term:vevraa) rule (91 FR 54234) and the [Section 503](#term:section-503) rule (91 FR 54482), both published 2026-08-21, took effect 2026-09-21; the Section 503 rule rescinds the disability self-identification requirement and the 7% utilization goal [309](#cite:309) [310](#cite:310).

title: Section 503 rule's part 60-30 amendment effective
what: Amendatory instruction 1 of the [Section 503](#term:section-503) rule, amending 41 CFR part 60-30, takes effect 2026-12-21 [310](#cite:310).

title: FAC 2026-01 currency of FAR 22.1803 E-Verify prescription
what: At FAC 2026-01, effective 2026-03-13, [FAR 22.1803](#term:e-verify) reads 'all solicitations and contracts that exceed \$150,000' with the outside-U.S., under-120-day and COTS exceptions [307](#cite:307).
